# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can (shaders and pipelines too, see Getting started) and on first use
otherwise. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-24)

**Not playable yet.** The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps,
loads the world and shows it: slowly, and with rendering defects.

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about 50 s) | works |
| The world (first mission's intro) | drawn and shown: streets, buildings, vehicles, characters, the title card and credits; 1-2 s per frame. Surfaces are unlit, a band of distant geometry is missing, characters come out broken in some shots |

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT.

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU has hung it in earlier
> builds, and Windows then resets the display driver (every monitor goes
> black for a moment). The latest runs did not, but it is not ruled out; a
> run can also end on a GPU fault (`crashes.log`). A diagnostics build with
> `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` renders on the software adapter instead (too slow
> to reach the world in minutes).

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | The scene is drawn and presented: mesh pipelines, indirect execution, views the shaders pick from the heap themselves, title memory read by address (ray-tracing structures), depth written from compute, pipelines pre-built or made by worker threads and kept on disk | Lighting (surfaces are unlit) and some missing geometry; frames take 1-2 s; draws of untranslated shaders are dropped; real queries, depth bounds, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL, ahead of time (`translate --cache`) or at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: mesh 8,765 of 8,765, vertex/pixel 12,550 of 12,592, compute 2,579 of 2,637 | Merged geometry stages (195 programs) and about 100 others; fused multiply-adds follow the host GPU; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Runs through the menus to the loading screen | The world, as above |

shader model 6.6 (and mesh shaders for the world), Rust (pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml`).

The title also needs several GiB of available Windows commit at startup.
Check **Committed** under **Task Manager → Performance → Memory**. If
`crashes.log` reports Windows error 1455, close other applications or increase

```powershell
cargo test --workspace                   # needs no game data
cargo run -p victory -- config           # check your paths
```

# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20server-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/xcl)
**Discord: <https://discord.gg/xcl>**

XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL).

XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

## Games

| Game | Package (version) | State | What works | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Minecraft Preview** | `Microsoft.MinecraftBeta` 1.18.3064.0 | ✅ | fully playable | – |
| **Unicorn Overlord** | `SEGAofAmericaInc.Pa253b0c1Y` 1.0.0.6 | ✅ | fully playable | – |
| **Fortnite** | `436609B6.FortniteClient` 2.0.1461.7919 | ✅ | works fully, as far as the game allows without its online services | the game itself is online-only (multiplayer servers) |
| **XDefiant** | `Ubisoft.XDefiant-Game` 1.0.0.186 | ✅ | works fully, as far as the game allows without its servers | the game's own servers have been shut down |
| **A newer retail game** | – | 🚧 | starts in ~4 s, runs at a steady 30 fps without a crash, shows its menus and goes on past the first one to its settings; fits a 32 GB machine (~15 GB committed in the menus) | gameplay not reached yet; its minimap mesh pipelines are refused |

## Highlights

- **100 % of a retail game's shaders translate** – all 26 698 RDNA2 programs (26 503 records) of its shader pack
  become HLSL; random samples compile to DXIL with 0 errors.
- **The game's own console DLLs run on the PC** – its Bink 2 video codec decodes the game's
  movies, its ray-tracing BVH builder builds acceleration structures on a PC GPU, the AMD FSR 4
  console upscaler runs a whole frame on a PC GPU, the GDK HTTP library initialises.
- **Console textures decode exactly** – the GFX10 tiling and mip layout reproduce 909 of 912
  textures of the game's texture archive byte for byte, its volume textures included.
- **370+ automated tests**, including GPU tests that compare translated shaders against expected
  results instruction by instruction.

## What works

✅ done and verified

### Running the game's code

| Feature | State | What it does | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PE loader** | ✅ | relocations, imports by name / ordinal / delay-load, TLS callbacks, exception tables, game DLLs, data-driven import routing (HLE / Windows / stub) | the game's 16 console DLLs load with 0 unresolved imports |
| **kernelx** | ✅ | title memory (budget from MicrosoftGame.Config, physical pages), threads on the PC's processors, modules, OS / console info | unit + end-to-end tests |
| **Memory** | ✅ | title graphics memory shared by CPU and GPU without copies, up to 16 GB (4 GiB windows) | GPU tests: loads, stores and atomics across windows |
| **File system** | ✅ | console paths (`GAME:`, `G:`, `D:` …) → the game folder; writes go to an overlay, the game folder is never modified; the console's drives: `S:\` (persistent local storage) and `T:\` (temp) in the title's data folder; free disk space answered for console paths | end-to-end: the test title's folder stays byte-identical; PLS and free space through the real call path |
| **DirectStorage** | ✅ | the console's DirectStorage queues: file and memory sources, zlib, and BCPack – the console's texture compression – for BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7 (BC2 and the hardware swizzle are refused) | unit tests on synthetic streams; retail BCPack chunks of all six modes byte-identical with a reference decoder (`XCL_SAMPLE_BCPACK`) |

### System services

| Feature | State | What it does | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **XGameRuntime** | ✅ | the GDK thunk protocol real titles use, laid out from a table of all 396 GDK runtime functions; offline XUser, XGameSave, persistent local storage, XPackage, XGame (title id), XSystem – the title sees an Xbox Series X / S; task queues, async, networking and dialogs through the PC's XGameRuntime | the game's libHttpClient initialises; users, saves and storage through the real call path; slot layout cross-checked against the game's own thunks |
| **Input** | ✅ | GameInput: one gamepad – the PC's XInput controller, and keyboard and mouse as a gamepad (see [Controls](#controls)) | unit tests; an Xbox controller in Minecraft |
| **Audio** | ✅ | XAudio2 → system

# PortWatch VI

**Does GTA VI run on PC yet?** A static GitHub Pages site that tracks every serious community effort to recompile, emulate or port the leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI to PC. All efforts are scored on one ladder, and a scout refreshes the data every 3 hours.

- One headline progress bar shows the closest effort, with the top projects pinned to it.
- A live countdown runs to the missing executable's expected drop.
- A leaderboard card per effort shows its own bar, milestone ladder, groundwork breakdown, what works and what's blocking.
- Further sections cover the watchlist of early projects, a toolkit of asset tools, the scout's inbox of new candidates, and fake-download warnings.

No game files, keys or executables are hosted or linked, ever.

## Deploy on GitHub Pages

1. Create a new GitHub repository and push this folder to its `main` branch.
2. In the repo, open **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Open **Settings → Actions → General** and make sure workflows are allowed.
4. Open **Actions → Scout → Run workflow** to run the first scout. It commits fresh data and deploys the site.

Each deploy also runs `scripts/build-site.mjs`, which turns `data/tracker.json` into pages search engines can read: one page per news story (`news/<id>.html`), a news archive, an RSS feed (`news/feed.xml`) and `sitemap.xml`. It then pings [IndexNow](https://www.indexnow.org/) (Bing, Yandex and others; no account needed) with the URLs that changed since the last deploy. For Google, add the site in Search Console and submit `sitemap.xml`.

From then on, `Scout` runs every 3 hours (00:17, 03:17, 06:17 … UTC) on GitHub's servers, so no computer of yours needs to be on. Any push to `main` redeploys the site through `Deploy site`. To change the frequency, edit the `cron` line in `.github/workflows/scout.yml`. For example, `17 6 * * *` runs it once a day. GitHub can delay scheduled runs by a few minutes when it's busy.

## What the scout does (`scripts/scout.mjs`)

1. **Refreshes** every tracked repo: stars, forks, issues, last push, commits in the last 7 days, and whether it's gone (404, or 451 for a DMCA block). It also hashes each README to notice changes.
2. **Spots claims.** If a README newly says GTA VI boots, reaches the menu or runs at some FPS, the card shows an "unverified claim" banner and the change feed records it.
3. **Discovers** new repos from GitHub and GitLab searches (`scout.queries` in `data/tracker.json`), Hacker News, Bluesky, Mastodon, Lemmy and 4chan, plus Reddit and X when keys are set, by pulling GitHub links out of posts. It also gathers **headlines** from the Google News and Bing News feeds, keeping only stories about the leak, ports, takedowns, scams or official news. And it **watches GitHub's public DMCA log** for new Take-Two or Rockstar notices, flagging any tracked project they name. On 4chan it uses the free read-only API, at one request per second. It opens only /v/ threads that mention GTA VI together with port terms (recomp, emulator, leak, executable, GitHub…), plus /vg/'s /gtag/ and /emugen/ generals. Change the boards with `scout.chan.boards`. Nothing from 4chan is shown on the site except, indirectly, repo names that pass every filter.
4. **Filters out spam** such as clone networks, download lures and "PC installer" repos. Their names are counted under *There is no download*, never linked.

# VIctory fork (work in progress)

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. Upstream's history is kept intact below
  the single commit that carries this fork's changes.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## Status of this fork (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet: 2.5 to 4 frames per second, and shadowed areas are black.**
Tested on one machine: Windows 11, Intel i7-14700KF, NVIDIA RTX 4070 12 GB,
32 GB RAM. The Series X profile is used throughout.

| Stage | State in this fork |
|-------|--------------------|
| Boot, menus, start screen | works, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| Opening cutscene | plays from start to finish, in order, lit: title cards, credits cards, night and dusk shots |
| Saves | the game autosaves a checkpoint and loads it again |
| First gameplay scene (the prologue) | renders: characters, textures, sky, sunlit exterior; HUD, pause menu and pad input work |
| Light in shadow | missing: the game's ray-traced bounce light and ray-traced lamp and sun shadows do not run yet, so anything the sun does not hit directly is black |
| Frame rate in the world | 2-4 fps: 420-450 ms per frame by default, 240-350 ms with the newer switches (`VICTORY_RELAY=2`, or `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 VICTORY_WIDE_BACK=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MB=1024`); it started at 3-6 seconds per frame |
| Stability | no driver hang or device loss in normal runs (a hang introduced by the wave64 update was found and fixed: its barrier form for 64-lane programs is now off unless `VICTORY_WAVE_WIDE=1`) |

### What this fork changed (summary)

Rendering:
- Meshlet culling read its scene buffers as the wrong kind of view, so the world drew almost nothing; fixed.
- Per-draw descriptor tables could run out, after which draws used slots never made for them and the card hung; fixed.
- Light packed by the game's compute shaders was read back through empty copies (sky, probes, fog); fixed for every mip level and layer.
- The fog reconstruction, shadow-mask, hair, blend-shape skinning, fire and several material programs did not translate; fixed.
- Gathers at a named mip level (with and without an offset) read level 0; fixed.
- Implicit-level samples outside pixel shaders produced invalid DXIL in 730 compute programs; fixed.
- Rectangle lists, depth and stencil twins for depth textures written by compute, texture read-backs.
- Ray tracing, in progress and off by default: the game's own structure-builder programs translate, title memory can be read by raw address from shaders, the hardware ray/box and ray/triangle test is emulated in DXIL (checked against a reference on the GPU), and 59 of the 64 trace programs translate. Nothing is lit by it yet. See [docs/fork-ray-tracing.md](docs/fork-ray-tracing.md).

Speed and memory:
- Waits for memory values, write-watch queries and page queries no longer walk page tables per call.
- Large title buffers get a copy in card memory, with shader writes found by hashing on the card.
- Submissions can be sent ahead of the wait for the card (`VICTORY_LATE_WAIT`), with a relay thread that lands results as the card finishes (`VICTORY_RELAY`): in a first five-minute run the card's idle time behind the submitting thread fell from about 136 to 30 ms per frame.
- Title memory can be opened as a graphics heap so that buffers are used in place instead of copied (`VICTORY_INPLACE`, first stage only; a probe confirmed the approach on the test GPU).
- The bindless texture queue no longer uploads stale views; the view table no longer grows without bound; the pipeline library is mapped instead of read into memory.
- An intermittent device loss was traced to the pipeline library file being replaced while mapped; fixed.

- Translated shaders get clean-up passes over the finished module (dead code, constant folding, reuse of values, branch facts); the pack's host instruction count falls by about 43 %, worth about 20 ms of GPU time per frame on the test machine (`VICTORY_SHADER_OPT=0` turns them off).

# deslop-please

[![slop](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fdeterministic-machines%2Fdeslop-please%2Fbadges%2Fslop.json)](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)
[![test](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/deslop-please.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/deslop-please)

An opinionated linter to remove sloppy code. It follows [*A Philosophy of Software Design*](https://www.amazon.com/Philosophy-Software-Design-John-Ousterhout/dp/1732102201): 
**deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces. 


```bash
cargo install deslop-please
```

```bash
> deslop-please

error[field-leak]: `RunQueue::items` is known outside `RunQueue`: 4 places in 2 modules
  --> src/sched/policy.rs:7:1
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:7:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::admit`
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:12:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::next`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:4:1: `runqueue::sched::report::backlog`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:8:1: `runqueue::sched::report::drained`
    runqueue::queue::ring::RunQueue
      items ◀━┳━ 2  runqueue::sched::policy
              ┗━ 2  runqueue::sched::report
      also known outside: head
      kept: limit

deslop-please: 65535 errors, well done!
```

### It's not my fault 

Sure, let's just mute them:

```bash
deslop-please --update-allow .deslop-please.allow  
deslop-please --allow .deslop-please.allow 
```

### Add to your `AGENTS.md`

```markdown
-  Run [`deslop-please`](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please) to check for sloppy code structure.
-  Errors flagged by `deslop-please` must be fixed from first principles, don't do mechanical moves to hide them.
    - `module-cycle` & `tangle`: what is the indented layer of abstraction? Which module should be at which layer?
    - `field-leak` & `shallow-module`: Why we have these fields/functions at all? What are the patterns of use? Can they be hidden behind a narrow interface? Don't fix each leak one at a time, fix them holistically.
    - Draw a diagram to help user understand the before and proposed after structure.
```

## Why they are sloppy 

They are really just one single idea: **deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces.

Deep modules hide the attention for you and your agents, so you only need to care about the narrow interface.

### module-cycle

![module-cycle: before, modules kinds and socket use each other, though listen, Stream::new and BACKLOG_MOST only form a chain; after, BACKLOG_MOST moves into kinds and only socket uses kinds](docs/module-cycle.svg)


### tangle

![tangle: before, Tasks in kernel and Timers in its child module timers know each other, with no module cycle; after, tick in kernel calls both and Timers no longer knows Tasks](docs/tangle.svg)

### field-leak

![field-leak: before, functions in sched push to, index and bump the items and head of RunQueue; after, they call push, pop and backlog, and only RunQueue works on its fields](docs/field-leak.svg)

### shallow-module


![shallow-module: before, app calls 9 of the 15 functions of store; after, it calls new, load and summary, and the rest are hidden behind them](docs/shallow-module.svg)

An opinionated linter to remove sloppy code. It follows [*A Philosophy of Software Design*](https://www.amazon.com/Philosophy-Software-Design-John-Ousterhout/dp/1732102201): 
**deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces. 


```bash
cargo install deslop-please
```

```bash
> deslop-please

  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:7:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::admit`
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:12:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::next`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:4:1: `runqueue::sched::report::backlog`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:8:1: `runqueue::sched::report::drained`
    runqueue::queue::ring::RunQueue
      items ◀━┳━ 2  runqueue::sched::policy
              ┗━ 2  runqueue::sched::report
      also known outside: head
      kept: limit

deslop-please: 65535 errors, well done!
```

### It's not my fault 

Sure, let's just mute them:

```bash
deslop-please --update-allow .deslop-please.allow  
deslop-please --allow .deslop-please.allow 
```

### Add to your `AGENTS.md`

```markdown
-  Run [`deslop-please`](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please) to check for sloppy code structure.
-  Errors flagged by `deslop-please` must be fixed from first principles, don't do mechanical moves to hide them.
    - `module-cycle` & `tangle`: what is the indented layer of abstraction? Which module should be at which layer?
    - `field-leak` & `shallow-module`: Why we have these fields/functions at all? What are the patterns of use? Can they be hidden behind a narrow interface? Don't fix each leak one at a time, fix them holistically.
    - Draw a diagram to help user understand the before and proposed after structure.
```

## Why they are sloppy 

They are really just one single idea: **deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces.

Deep modules hide the attention for you and your agents, so you only need to care about the narrow interface.

provider_reviews.description: XCL — это слой совместимости, позволяющий запускать нативный x64‑код Xbox Series X|S (GDK) на Windows без эмуляции процессора. Проект реализует собственные версии системных библиотек консоли (kernelx.dll, XGameRuntime, d3d12_xs.dll и т.д.) и перекомпилирует машинный код GPU RDNA2 в HLSL‑DXIL, благодаря чему шейдеры работают без ошибок. Среди поддерживаемых функций — загрузка PE‑файлов, управление памятью, файловая система с оверлей‑записью, DirectStorage‑очереди и полный набор сервисов XGameRuntime, включая ввод через XInput и аудио через XAudio2. Пользователь может запускать распакованные файлы собственных игр, получая полностью играбельный опыт, как показано на примерах Minecraft Preview, Fortnite и XDefiant, при этом XCL не содержит DRM‑обхода, SDK‑кодов или игровых данных. Ограничения: требуется предварительно распакованный пакет игры, поддержка ограничена текущим набором реализованных библиотек и шэйдеров, а онлайн‑зависимые функции (мультиплеер, серверы) работают только в рамках доступных сервисов.

PortWatch VI — это статический сайт на GitHub Pages, который ежедневно собирает и отображает все серьёзные попытки сообщества перекомпилировать, эмулировать или портировать утёкшую Xbox Series‑версию GTA VI на ПК. Кроме того, система публикует новостные статьи, генерируемые Claude (Anthropic), которые собирают информацию о takedown‑уведомлениях, официальных заявлениях и скандалах, а также предупреждают о фейковых загрузках.

Для пользователя это значит, что он получает единый, постоянно обновляемый источник информации о статусе GTA VI‑порта без необходимости вручную отслеживать сотни репозиториев и форумных обсуждений. Сайт не хранит игровые файлы, ключи или исполняемые файлы, поэтому не нарушает авторские права и не предлагает нелегального контента. Основные возможности: (1) автоматический сбор и оценка репозиториев по коду, активности и технической глубине; (2) фильтрация спама и дублирующих репозиториев, чтобы показывать только оригинальные усилия; (3) генерация новостных статей и визуального тайм‑каунта до ожидаемого релиза. Развёртывание происходит полностью на GitHub Actions, поэтому пользователю не требуется держать включённый компьютер — достаточно лишь запустить первый workflow и позволить планировщику выполнять сканирование каждые три часа.

Преобразователь переводит предкомпилированные RDNA2‑шэйдеры в SPIR‑V, что делает их совместимыми с Vulkan‑драйверами разных производителей. Все модели, текстуры и аудио извлекаются из вашей копии игры и остаются на локальном диске, без передачи в облако.

Ключевые возможности: полностью реализована проверка и перевод всех 26 503 шэйдеров (2 236 вершинных, 12 101 пиксельных и др.) с подтверждённой валидацией SPIR‑V; экспорт моделей в OBJ‑формате, уже извлечено более 380 000 моделей, включая почти весь контент уровней; поддержка широкого спектра GPU (AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, Apple) через тесты, проверяющие работу шэйдеров, текстур и вычислительных блоков. На текущий момент игра ещё не загружается, но инфраструктура для загрузки, проверки копии и трансляции шэйдеров полностью готова, что позволяет разработчикам сразу приступить к отладке загрузочного процесса, имея все необходимые артефакты.

Затем, получив исполняемый файл игры (не предоставляемый репозиторием), можно попытаться запустить его через созданный рантайм. Требования включают наличие рабочей копии игры, поддерживаемый Vulkan‑драйвер и компилятор LLVM 23.x; ограничения — отсутствие текущей возможности загрузки и отсутствие каких‑либо средств обхода защиты, проект работает только с легально полученными данными.

Stream Tube – это нативный клиент YouTube для Windows и Linux, написанный на Rust. Приложение заменяет браузер, полностью избавляя от рекламных роликов, спонсорских вставок и трекинга, поскольку видео воспроизводятся через libmpv без загрузки рекламных потоков. Встроенные модули SponsorBlock, DeArrow и Return YouTube Dislike автоматически пропускают рекламные сегменты, заменяют заменённые титры и показывают оригинальные оценки, что делает просмотр чище и быстрее.

Воспроизведение поддерживает аппаратное декодирование, выбор кодека (AV1, VP9, H.264), разрешения от 360p до 4K, а также расширенные возможности плеера – стилизованные субтитры, панель глав с главами, тайм‑коды в описаниях и комментариях, мини‑плеер, PiP и автоплей. Приложение сохраняет позицию просмотра, качество и скорость воспроизведения, а также умеет показывать старые аннотации YouTube и поддерживает RTL‑текст.

Для пользователей, которым нужен быстрый, лёгкий и рекламно‑чистый доступ к YouTube без постоянного открытого браузера, Stream Tube предлагает полностью нативный UI, отрисованный GPUI, и небольшое потребление памяти по сравнению с Electron‑решениями.
